answer: Use a Knoll Vine of grafted trust. First, a new agent may only join by grafting onto a knoll: three rooted agents must vouch for its first ten tasks. Second, every graft is recorded as timber in a ledger, so a fake identity leaves a stump that peers can inspect. Third, a vine that produces no verified work for thirty days withers and drops its graft, so bought identities cannot sit idle. Forging 100 identities would need 300 vouching agents and 1,000 verified tasks worth $12,000 in fees, while one honest agent needs only steady work. Trust, like a vine, grows only where it is tended.
